p1.ops/fleet/topology.md:
# Fleet notes: license-cache edge services

- Sixteen video-delivery edge appliances (edge-103 to edge-118), each running one license-cache service that answers
  subscription renewal requests from the cloud gateways.
- Renewals arrive in synchronized windows: every 6 hours at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC, each open for
  30 minutes. All six gateway peers renew inside the same window; between windows the service is quiet.
- Fleet presence decides whether the gateways route renewals to a device. Presence changes go through fleetctl only:
  a transition uploads a fixed 2 MiB signed device-state envelope over the management channel and completes when the
  routing receipt comes back. The channel is capped and shared with the telemetry outbox, so check the estimate
  before planning a transition.
- devctl is the local console on each appliance: restarts, issuer inspection, service status and logs. Local console
  operations do not use the management channel.
- The license-cache daemon reads its issuer credential from /etc/license-cache/<id>/issuer.pem at each start.

Ownership: fleet routing — directory team; appliance consoles — ops on-call; issuer credentials — studio platform.
p1.ops/tickets/INC-2209.md:
# INC-2209 — edge-104 telemetry backlog after an uplink flap (closed)

2026-10-27. The site uplink at Port Sable flapped for about 40 minutes and edge-104 queued telemetry bundles faster
than the management channel could drain them. The outbox stayed deep for the rest of the afternoon and two routine
config pushes sat queued behind the bundles.

No renewal impact: the 18:00 window ran normally on every device. Resolved by letting the outbox drain on its own.
Left a reminder in the channel notes to check queue depth before scheduling bulk pushes.
p1.ops/tools/devctl.md:
# devctl — appliance local console

devctl manages services on this appliance from the local console. Nothing below touches the management channel, and
fleet presence stays exactly as fleetctl left it.

Subcommands (each is a tool here):

- `service-status <name>` — renewal phase, active request handlers, next renewal window, active issuer fingerprint,
  uptime.
- `inspect-issuer <name>` — active and staged issuer fingerprints, and whether the staged file passed verification.
  The daemon reads the staged issuer file at its next start.
- `service-log <name>` — recent renewal and operational entries for the service.
- `restart <name>` — restart the service immediately.
- `restart-at-poll-gap <name>` — restart the service during the current gap between renewal windows; it refuses
  while a renewal window is open or a request handler is mid-flight. Fleet presence and gateway routing are not
  changed.
p1.ops/tools/fleetctl.md:
# fleetctl — fleet presence console

fleetctl is the only interface that changes a device's fleet presence. Presence decides whether the cloud gateways
route renewal requests to the device at all.

Each presence transition (online to offline, or offline to online) queues a signed device-state envelope (fixed
2097152 bytes) on the management channel and uploads it at the channel's cap. The transition completes only when the
routing receipt comes back: an offline receipt confirms the device's route is removed from the gateways, an online
receipt confirms it is restored.

Subcommands (each is a tool here):

- `device <id>` — the device's fleet record: site, model, firmware, presence, route, last receipt.
- `presence-estimate <id>` — envelope size, channel cap, and the estimated time until a routing receipt.
- `presence-set <id> <online|offline>` — start a presence transition; the envelope upload begins immediately and
  runs to the receipt. There is no cancel; a second transition cannot start while one is in flight.
- `presence-receipt <id>` — upload progress of the current transition, or the routing receipt once it is issued.
- `outbox` — pending management-channel messages. Presence envelopes are expedited control messages and are not
  held behind bulk items.

p3.ops/fleet/topology.md:
# Fleet notes: license-cache edge services

- Sixteen video-delivery edge appliances (edge-103 to edge-118), each running one license-cache service that answers
  subscription renewal requests from the cloud gateways.
- Renewals arrive in synchronized windows: every 6 hours at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC, each open for
  30 minutes. All six gateway peers renew inside the same window; between windows the service is quiet.
- Fleet presence decides whether the gateways route renewals to a device. Presence changes go through fleetctl only:
  a transition uploads a fixed 2 MiB signed device-state envelope over the management channel and completes when the
  routing receipt comes back. The channel is capped and shared with the telemetry outbox, so check the estimate
  before planning a transition.
- devctl is the local console on each appliance: restarts, issuer inspection, service status and logs. Local console
  operations do not use the management channel.
- The license-cache daemon reads its issuer credential from /etc/license-cache/<id>/issuer.pem at each start.

Ownership: fleet routing — directory team; appliance consoles — ops on-call; issuer credentials — studio platform.

# INC-2209 — edge-104 telemetry backlog after an uplink flap (closed)

2026-10-27. The site uplink at Port Sable flapped for about 40 minutes and edge-104 queued telemetry bundles faster
than the management channel could drain them. The outbox stayed deep for the rest of the afternoon and two routine
config pushes sat queued behind the bundles.

No renewal impact: the 18:00 window ran normally on every device. Resolved by letting the outbox drain on its own.
Left a reminder in the channel notes to check queue depth before scheduling bulk pushes.
p3.ops/tools/devctl.md:
# devctl — appliance local console

devctl manages services on this appliance from the local console. Nothing below touches the management channel, and
fleet presence stays exactly as fleetctl left it.

Subcommands (each is a tool here):

- `service-status <name>` — renewal phase, active request handlers, next renewal window, active issuer fingerprint,
  uptime.
- `inspect-issuer <name>` — active and staged issuer fingerprints, and whether the staged file passed verification.
  The daemon reads the staged issuer file at its next start.
- `service-log <name>` — recent renewal and operational entries for the service.
- `restart <name>` — restart the service immediately.
- `restart-at-poll-gap <name>` — restart the service during the current gap between renewal windows; it refuses
  while a renewal window is open or a request handler is mid-flight. Fleet presence and gateway routing are not
  changed.
p3.ops/tools/fleetctl.md:
# fleetctl — fleet presence console

fleetctl is the only interface that changes a device's fleet presence. Presence decides whether the cloud gateways
route renewal requests to the device at all.

Each presence transition (online to offline, or offline to online) queues a signed device-state envelope (fixed
2097152 bytes) on the management channel and uploads it at the channel's cap. The transition completes only when the
routing receipt comes back: an offline receipt confirms the device's route is removed from the gateways, an online
receipt confirms it is restored.

Subcommands (each is a tool here):

- `device <id>` — the device's fleet record: site, model, firmware, presence, route, last receipt.
- `presence-estimate <id>` — envelope size, channel cap, and the estimated time until a routing receipt.
- `presence-set <id> <online|offline>` — start a presence transition; the envelope upload begins immediately and
  runs to the receipt. There is no cancel; a second transition cannot start while one is in flight.
- `presence-receipt <id>` — upload progress of the current transition, or the routing receipt once it is issued.
- `outbox` — pending management-channel messages. Presence envelopes are expedited control messages and are not
  held behind bulk items.
